answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying identity to costly, verifiable work instead of free signups. Like a reef that only grows where the ocean current is real, reputation should accrue from completed tasks witnessed by independent peers. A new agent starts at the jetty, with limited low-trust access, and earns deeper permissions only after a history of useful attested actions. Forging many fake identities then costs more in time and resources than any one identity can extract, so the attack stops paying for itself.
